chapter: Learning piano, dancing and Alphonso Trent
title: Ella B. Moore's 1925 road show and watching Cow Cow Davenport and Jesse Crump
summary: Mrs. Moore tells him he will be a musician and invites him on a summer road show; he haunts the theater when pianists like Jesse Crump come through.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

PRICE: 5.
DM: 25...
PRICE: 1925. Then I by this time was very, very close to Ella B. Moore. Well, I could dance and this gave me the opportunity--she had a little amateur show of kids; they were pretty good, though, you know, do little drama things and chorus girls and, you know--so in 1925 she said to me, "Willie, you know I think you're going to be a musician." Right then I says, "Why?" She says, "I hear you always fooling around." Wherever I saw a piano--they were so rare there--that wherever I saw one I ran right to it, you know, so she says, "I hear you always fooling around my piano. How would you like to go out this summer on a little road show. So what happened--show people used to wear shoes without laces, you know, they were...you know, you take a shoe horn and put the shoe on, but it was--just like these shoes that I have now--they have this thing on it, but it was no top, you know, they had a top but there wasn't anything on it. So the first thing I did when she said that was to go buy me a pair of those shoes like the road shows. And I'd stand around the theater when, say, Cow Cow Davenport came to town and Jesse Crump, who was my favorite, who played for Ida Cox. When Jesse came to town I would always...I would be

at the theater when they come and I would stay until they left. I watched everything and tried to just be a professional person in that way. And then, actually I was improving on my piano playing. And people would let me play now that...around at the house-rent parties I was, you know, popular. Very popular. That was in 1925, and I went up...we went up to Okmulgee, Oklahoma. This is where I first met Oscar Pettiford.
